subject.title: Rebrand text-substitution filter on tool-call arguments silently misroutes file ops

question: Should plugin text transforms be allowed to rewrite structured tool-call argument strings, or should path/tool-bearing arguments be exempt by default with any rewrite opt-in?
rationale: This choice defines public plugin/backend text-transform semantics and trades off privacy/terminology transform coverage against silent filesystem misrouting and user data loss.

options.title: Exempt path/tool-bearing arguments by default
options.body: Keep cosmetic prompt/output transforms but skip filesystem-looking tool argument strings unless a narrower, explicit API opts into argument rewriting.

options.title: Keep current argument transform semantics
options.body: Preserve broad plugin transform power and require plugins or `before_tool_call` hooks to avoid unsafe path rewrites themselves.

options.title: Design a new transform scope contract
options.body: Add explicit transform scopes for prompt, display, structured arguments, and persistence before changing runtime behavior.

recommendation.title: Exempt path/tool-bearing arguments by default
recommendation.body: Keep cosmetic prompt/output transforms but skip filesystem-looking tool argument strings unless a narrower, explicit API opts into argument rewriting.

likelyOwner.reason: `steipete` introduced the text-transform surface and is the strongest current history signal for choosing the durable plugin/runtime boundary.
